curriculum.lesson_evidence: Evaluating a game means judging how well it works using criteria such as safety, fairness, fun and skill practice. Collect evidence (scores, observations, player comments), find strengths and problems and then change one rule at a time to improve it. After the change, play again to see whether it worked.

lesson.child_mission: Evaluating a game means judging how well it works using criteria such as safety, fairness, fun and skill practice. lesson.extension: Apply the same idea to a new game or situation, then compare two choices for safety and inclusion.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A game's evaluation shows low fairness because the same player always scores. Suggest one rule change and the evidence you would collect to test it.

FEEDBACK
Rule: everyone must pass to a new player before a shot. Evidence: count how many different players score in the next round and ask the players whether it felt fairer.

WATCH FOR
Believing that changing many rules at once will make a game better. Change one thing at a time so you can tell what worked.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Evaluate a game you play using the four criteria with scores from 1 to 5 and evidence. Change one rule, replay and record the new scores. Write a sentence about whether your change helped.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Evaluate a game you play using the four criteria with scores from 1 to 5 and evidence. Change one rule, replay and record the new scores. Write a sentence about whether your change helped. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original demonstration: Example: evaluating 'Four-pass goal'. Safety: 4 out of 5 (some bumping). Fairness: 3 (one team stronger). Fun: 5. Skill practice: 4. Evidence: the score was 6 to 1. Change: mix the teams. Replay: 4 to 3 and both teams enjoyed it. The change improved fairness.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Believing that changing many rules at once will make a game better. Change one thing at a time so you can tell what worked. Correction: Rule: everyone must pass to a new player before a shot. Evidence: count how many different players score in the next round and ask the players whether it felt fairer.
